subproblem.title: Locality of approximate tangent spaces for nested sets (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2); Ch. 1, 3.6)
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open and let A ⊆ B ⊆ U be Borel sets with H^n(B ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U. Then for H^n-a.e. x ∈ A and every linear subspace Q of ℝ^P: B has approximate tangent space Q at x (Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4; HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q) if and only if A has approximate tangent space Q at x.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U A B : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet B → A ⊆ B → B ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (B ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict A), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the proof of Theorem 1.6 '⇒' (chapter-03.txt lines 86–144), which compares ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M)} f dH^n with ∫_{η_{x,λ}(N_j)} f dH^n by the Upper Density Theorem of Ch. 1, 3.6 (chapter-01.txt lines 700–712). Notation: η_{x,λ}(z) = λ^{−1}(z − x); H^n = μHE[n]; HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q means dim Q = n and ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as λ ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). Simon's H^n (SimonGMT simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n) and μHE[n] are positive constant multiples of μH[n], so they have the same null sets; only this is used.

1. (Vanishing density of B ∖ A at a.e. point of A.) For j ≥ 1 let V_j := {z ∈ U : |z| < j, dist(z, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 1/j} (V_j := ball(0, j) if U = ℝ^P). Each V_j is open with compact closure in U, and ⋃_j V_j = U. A'_j := (B ∖ A) ∩ V_j is Borel with H^n(A'_j) ≤ H^n(B ∩ closure(V_j)) < ∞. By the Upper Density Theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6, applied to the Borel regular measure H^n and the set A'_j of finite measure; SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6 and simon_remark_3_7_hausdorff), Θ^{*n}(H^n, A'_j, x) := limsup_{ρ↓0} H^n(A'_j ∩ B_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρ^n) = 0 for H^n-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P ∖ A'_j. Let N₀ := ⋃_j {x ∈ A ∩ V_j : Θ^{*n}(H^n, A'_j, x) ≠ 0}; since A ∩ V_j ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ A'_j, N₀ is H^n-null. For x ∈ A ∖ N₀ choose j with x ∈ V_j; for small ρ, B_ρ(x) ⊆ V_j and so H^n((B ∖ A) ∩ B_ρ(x)) = H^n(A'_j ∩ B_ρ(x)). (The density quotient may be taken with closed or open balls: H^n(A'_j ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ H^n(A'_j ∩ closedBall(x, ρ)).) Hence
 (†) lim_{ρ↓0} ρ^{−n} H^n((B ∖ A) ∩ B_ρ(x)) = 0 for every x ∈ A ∖ N₀.

2. (Comparison of blow-ups.) Fix x ∈ A ∖ N₀ and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_R(0) (R > 0), and choose λ₀ > 0 with closedBall(x, λ₀R) ⊆ U. For 0 < λ < λ₀ the map η := η_{x,λ} is an injective affine similarity, so η(B) is the disjoint union of the Borel sets η(A) and η(B ∖ A), and for Borel S ⊆ ℝ^P, H^n(η(S) ∩ B_R(0)) = λ^{−n} H^n(S ∩ B_{λR}(x)) (translation invariance and H^n(cS) = |c|^n H^n(S)); for S ⊆ B this is finite because closedBall(x, λR) is a compact subset of U. Hence f is integrable on η(B), η(A) and η(B ∖ A),
 ∫_{η(B)} f dH^n − ∫_{η(A)} f dH^n = ∫_{η(B∖A)} f dH^n, and
 |∫_{η(B∖A)} f dH^n| ≤ sup|f| · λ^{−n} H^n((B ∖ A) ∩ B_{λR}(x)) = sup|f| · R^n (λR)^{−n} H^n((B ∖ A) ∩ B_{λR}(x)) → 0 as λ ↓ 0, by (†).

3. (Conclusion.) Therefore, for x ∈ A ∖ N₀ and every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), ∫_{η_{x,λ}(B)} f dH^n converges to a limit L as λ ↓ 0 if and only if ∫_{η_{x,λ}(A)} f dH^n converges to L. The requirement dim Q = n is the same on both sides. So for every x ∈ A ∖ N₀ and every Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q. Since A is Borel and N₀ is H^n-null, this holds for μHE[n].restrict A-almost every x.
proof_key_steps: Exhaust U by open V_j ⊂⊂ U and apply the Upper Density Theorem to (B ∖ A) ∩ V_j: ρ^{−n}H^n((B ∖ A) ∩ B_ρ(x)) → 0 for H^n-a.e. x ∈ A.
At such x the blow-ups of B and of A differ by η_{x,λ}(B ∖ A), whose H^n-measure inside B_R(0) is λ^{−n}H^n((B ∖ A) ∩ B_{λR}(x)) → 0.
Hence the limits in Definition 1.4 coincide for B and A.

audit.reason: The finite-measure exhaustion permits the upper-density theorem. Similarity scaling makes the blow-up integral differences vanish, proving both directions for every Q outside one null set. No rectifiability assumption or circular locality argument is used.

subproblem.title: Step 1 of Corollary 7.5.11: basic facts in the codimension-one setting and the vacuous case n = 0
subproblem.statement: Let n, k ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^{n+k} be open, let N ∈ 𝒪 with orientation ξ_N (InClassO n U N ξ_N: N is an embedded C² (n+1)-dimensional submanifold oriented by ξ_N, (N̄∖N) ∩ U = ∅ and N ∩ U ≠ ∅), let E ⊆ N ∩ U, and let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) satisfy T = ∂[[E]] in U, i.e. T(ω) = ∫_E ⟨dω, ξ_N⟩ dH^{n+1} for ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (IsBoundaryOfRegion), and be minimizing in N ∩ U (IsMinimizingIn T (N ∩ U)). Then (i) k ≥ 1; (ii) spt T ⊆ N; (iii) ∂T = 0 in U (BoundaryVanishes T, which is vacuous for n = 0); (iv) if n = 0 then reg T = ∅.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n k : ℕ) (U N E : Set (Euclid (n + k))) (ξN : Euclid (n + k) → MultiVector (n + k) (n + 1)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → InClassO n U N ξN → E ⊆ N ∩ U → IsBoundaryOfRegion T E ξN → IsMinimizingIn T (N ∩ U) → 1 ≤ k ∧ T.support ⊆ N ∧ BoundaryVanishes T ∧ (n = 0 → regularSet T = ∅)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 1 (Simon 7.5, chapter-07.txt lines 746–780: the class 𝒪 and T = ∂[[E]] (5.1)); for n = 0 the parent's remark 'minimizing 0-currents vanish' is proved here in the form needed, reg T = ∅. Notation: H^d = μHE[d]; tsupport ω is the closed support of a form; Z(T) (zeroRegion) is the union of the open sets with compact closure in U on which T vanishes, and spt T = U ∖ Z(T); M_W is the mass of the contract (supremum of T(ω) over ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm ≤ 1 everywhere).

1. (k ≥ 1.) By InClassO, N ∩ U ≠ ∅; pick y ∈ N. The embedded-submanifold property of N (dimension n+1) at y gives V ⊆ ℝ^{n+1} open, W ∋ y open and ψ with ψ(V) = W ∩ N and Dψ(z) injective for every z ∈ V. As y ∈ W ∩ N = ψ(V), V ≠ ∅. For z ∈ V the injective linear map Dψ(z) : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^{n+k} forces n + 1 ≤ n + k (the dimension of the domain of an injective linear map is at most that of the codomain), so k ≥ 1.

2. (spt T ⊆ N.) Let x ∈ spt T, so x ∈ U, and suppose x ∉ N. Because (N̄∖N) ∩ U = ∅ and x ∈ U, x ∉ N̄. Since U is open and N̄ is closed, choose r > 0 with closedBall(x, r) ⊆ U ∖ N̄ and put W₀ := ball(x, r): W₀ is open and its closure is a compact subset of U. If ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) has tsupport ω ⊆ W₀, then tsupport(dω) ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W₀ (exterior differentiation does not enlarge the topological support), and E ⊆ N is disjoint from W₀; so dω(z) = 0 for every z ∈ E and T(ω) = ∫_E ξ_N(z)(dω(z)) dH^{n+1}(z) = ∫_E ξ_N(z)(0) dH^{n+1}(z) = 0. Thus T vanishes on W₀, so x ∈ Z(T), contradicting x ∈ spt T = U ∖ Z(T). Hence spt T ⊆ N.

3. (∂T = 0.) If n = 0, BoundaryVanishes T is True by definition. If n = m + 1 and φ ∈ 𝒟^m(U), then ∂T(φ) = T(dφ) = ∫_E ξ_N(z)(d(dφ)(z)) dH^{n+1}(z) = 0, because d(dφ) = 0 for a smooth form φ (Simon (6.1.12); SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_sq) and ξ_N(z) is linear. Hence T.boundary = 0.

4. (n = 0 implies reg T = ∅.) Let n = 0 and suppose, for a contradiction, that y ∈ reg T. As T is minimizing it is integer multiplicity; fix an IMRep R of T with carrier C, multiplicity θ (θ ≥ 1 on C) and orientation ξ_R. Facts in dimension 0: H^0 = μHE[0] = μH[0] and H^0({x}) = 1, so H^0(F) = #F for finite F (additivity over measurable singletons), a set of finite H^0-measure is finite, and an H^0-null set is empty. Let ε₀ be the 0-covector with ε₀() = 1; every 0-covector α equals α()·ε₀; the Euclidean coefficient norm of a 0-covector α is |α()| (the only index map Fin 0 → Fin P is the empty one, which is strictly monotone); a unit orientation ξ' of a 0-dimensional space (empty orthonormal frame) satisfies ξ'(α) = ±α() for all α.
 4.1 (Local form of T.) By the definition of reg T there are ρ > 0 with ball(y, ρ) ⊆ U, m ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}, a 0-dimensional embedded C¹ submanifold M ∋ y with orientation ξ, and T(ω) = m ∫_M ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH^0(x) whenever tsupport ω ⊆ ball(y, ρ). Since ℝ^0 is a single point, a chart (V_M, W_M, ψ) of M at y has W_M ∩ M = ψ(V_M) ⊆ {ψ(0)}, hence W_M ∩ M = {y}. Choose r ∈ (0, ρ) with ball(y, r) ⊆ W_M; then M ∩ ball(y, r) = {y}. Writing ξ(y)(α) = s·α() with s ∈ {1, −1}, we get, for every ω with tsupport ω ⊆ ball(y, r) (the integrand vanishes on M ∖ {y}, which lies outside ball(y, r), so it is supported on the single point y, of H^0-measure 1, and is integrable):
 (*) T(ω) = m·ξ(y)(ω(y)) = m s ω(y)().
 4.2 (C is locally finite and oriented at every point.) For compact K ⊆ U, H^0(C ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{C∩K} θ dH^0 < ∞, so C ∩ K is finite. The set of points of C where the orientation condition of R fails is H^0-null, hence empty: for every x ∈ C, ξ_R(x)(α) = s_x α() for all α, with s_x ∈ {1, −1}.
 4.3 (C ∩ ball(y, r) ⊆ {y}.) Let x ∈ C ∩ ball(y, r) with x ≠ y. By 4.2 choose s' > 0 with closedBall(x, s') ⊆ ball(y, r) ∖ {y} and C ∩ closedBall(x, s') = {x}. Let g ∈ C_c^∞(ball(x, s')) with 0 ≤ g ≤ 1 and g(x) = 1, and ω := g ε₀ ∈ 𝒟^0(U). By (*), T(ω) = m s g(y) = 0. By the representation, T(ω) = ∫_C θ ξ_R(g ε₀) dH^0 = θ(x) s_x g(x) H^0({x}) = ±θ(x) ≠ 0 (the integrand vanishes on C off the single point x, since g = 0 off ball(x, s') and C ∩ closedBall(x, s') = {x}; so it is integrable). Contradiction.
 4.4 (y ∈ C.) Otherwise C ∩ ball(y, r) = ∅ by 4.3, so T(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ ball(y, r); but for g ∈ C_c^∞(ball(y, r)) with g(y) = 1, (*) gives T(g ε₀) = m s ≠ 0.
 4.5 (The competitor S.) Let W := ball(y, r/2): it is open and its closure lies in closedBall(y, r/2), a compact subset of ball(y, r) ⊆ U. Define D ∈ 𝒟_0(U) by D(ω) := θ(y) ξ_R(y)(ω(y)); D is linear and sequentially continuous (if ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^0(U) then ω_j(y) → 0). Let S := T − D. Using y ∈ C and H^0({y}) = 1, S(ω) = ∫_C θ ξ_R(ω) dH^0 − θ(y) ξ_R(y)(ω(y)) = ∫_{C∖{y}} θ ξ_R(ω) dH^0 (the integrand is supported on the finite set C ∩ tsupport ω, by 4.2, hence integrable, and the integral over C splits as the integral over C ∖ {y} plus the atom at y). The triple R_S := (C ∖ {y}, θ, ξ_R) is an IMRep in U: C ∖ {y} is Borel and ⊆ U; it is countably 0-rectifiable as a subset of C (CountablyRectifiable.mono); θ is measurable, positive and locally integrable on it; ξ_R is a.e. strongly measurable for the restricted measure; and for every x ∈ C ∖ {y} the sets C and C ∖ {y} have the same approximate tangent spaces at x: if f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) has spt f ⊆ B_R(0) and 0 < λ < |x − y|/R, then η_{x,λ}(C) and η_{x,λ}(C ∖ {y}) differ only by the point (y − x)/λ, whose norm exceeds R, so f vanishes there and the integrands f·1_{η_{x,λ}(C)} and f·1_{η_{x,λ}(C∖{y})} coincide pointwise; hence the integrals in Definition 1.4 of Ch. 3 coincide for all small λ and have the same limits. Hence the orientation condition of R at x transfers to R_S, and S is integer multiplicity.
 4.6 (Minimality applies.) S − T = −D as currents. If x ∈ U ∖ {y}, a ball around x whose closure is a compact subset of U ∖ {y} is a region on which D, hence S − T, vanishes; so spt(S − T) ⊆ {y}, a compact set contained in (N ∩ U) ∩ W, because y ∈ spt T ⊆ N (step 2), y ∈ U and y ∈ W. For n = 0, SameBoundary S T holds by definition. By minimality of T in N ∩ U: M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S).
 4.7 (M_W(S) = 0.) Let tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊆ ball(y, r). For z ∈ C ∖ {y} we have z ∉ ball(y, r) by 4.3, so ω(z) = 0 and S(ω) = 0. Every admissible value is ofReal 0, so M_W(S) = 0.
 4.8 (M_W(T) ≥ 1.) Take g ∈ C_c^∞(W) with 0 ≤ g ≤ 1 and g(y) = 1, and ω := σ g ε₀ with σ := sign(m s) ∈ {1, −1}. The Euclidean coefficient norm of ω(z) is g(z) ≤ 1 and tsupport ω ⊆ W, so ω is admissible for M_W(T), and by (*) T(ω) = m s σ = |m| ≥ 1. Hence M_W(T) ≥ 1 > 0 = M_W(S), contradicting 4.6. Therefore reg T = ∅ when n = 0.
proof_key_steps: An injective chart differential ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^{n+k} gives k ≥ 1.
T vanishes near points off N̄ because dω vanishes on E there; with (N̄∖N) ∩ U = ∅ this gives spt T ⊆ N.

For n = 0 a regular point y is an isolated atom of T: removing y from the carrier gives an integer multiplicity competitor S with spt(S − T) = {y} ⊆ N ∩ U ∩ W and M_W(S) = 0 < 1 ≤ M_W(T), contradicting minimality.

subproblem.title: Removable singular frontier: the cut-off argument for ∂T₁ = 0 (proof of Simon 7.5.11, corrected)
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, n = m + 1 ≥ 1, T, T₁ ∈ 𝒟_n(U), M₁ ⊆ ℝ^P and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n (n-vectors, MultiVector) such that: (h1) ∂T = 0 in U; (h2) T₁(ω) = ∫_{M₁} ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dH^n for ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U); (h3) |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ (operator norm) for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M₁ and all n-covectors α; (h4) every z ∈ M₁ has an open neighbourhood G and c ∈ ℝ with T₁(ω) = c·T(ω) whenever tsupport ω ⊆ G; (h5) for every compact K ⊆ U there is a compact Z with H^m(Z) = 0 (Mathlib μH[m]) and closure(M₁) ∩ K ⊆ M₁ ∪ Z; (h6) for every compact K ⊆ U there are C ∈ ℝ and r₁ > 0 with H^n(M₁ ∩ B_r(x)) ≤ C r^n for x ∈ K and 0 < r < r₁. Then ∂T₁ = 0 in U.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U M₁ : Set (Euclid P)) (T T₁ : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P (m + 1)), IsOpen U → T.boundary = 0 → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U (m + 1), T₁ ω = ∫ x in M₁, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) x) ∂μHE[m + 1]) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[m + 1].restrict M₁), ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) (m + 1), |ξ x α| ≤ ‖α‖) → (∀ z ∈ M₁, ∃ G : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen G ∧ z ∈ G ∧ ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ ω : TestFormOn U (m + 1), tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) ⊆ G → T₁ ω = c * T ω) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ Z : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact Z ∧ μH[(m : ℝ)] Z = 0 ∧ closure M₁ ∩ K ⊆ M₁ ∪ Z) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ C r₁ : ℝ, 0 < r₁ ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r < r₁ → μHE[m + 1] (M₁ ∩ ball x r) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * r ^ (m + 1))) → T₁.boundary = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: proof of Simon 7.5.11, (1)–(2) and the cut-off argument (chapter-07.txt lines 990–1016), parent proof step 4, with the parent's corrections: [D1] the cut-off is ζ = ∏_j (1 − φ_j), which vanishes near the singular points (printed: ζ = ∏ φ_j); [D2] the printed pointwise bound |d(ζω) − ζ dω| ≤ c|ω| Σ σ_j^{n−1} is replaced by an integrated estimate using the density bound (h6); [D3] the separation of M₁ from the rest of spt T (book: 'ζ ≡ 0 in a neighbourhood of spt T ∖ spt T₁') is done by a partition of unity subordinate to the neighbourhoods of (h4). Notation: for a k-form F, dF(x) is the alternation of DF(x), so ‖dF(x)‖ ≤ (k + 1) ‖DF(x)‖ and tsupport dF ⊆ tsupport F; 𝒟^k(U) are the smooth k-forms with compact support in U.
Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^m(U); we show ∂T₁(ω) = T₁(dω) = 0.

1. (Constants.) Let K := tsupport ω, a compact subset of U. By (h5) choose Z; replacing Z by Z ∩ K we may assume Z ⊆ K (Z ∩ K is compact, μH[m]-null, and closure(M₁) ∩ K ⊆ M₁ ∪ (Z ∩ K)). By (h6) for K choose C and r₁ > 0; we may assume C ≥ 0. Let δ₀ := min(1, r₁/2). Fix φ₀ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P) with 0 ≤ φ₀ ≤ 1, φ₀ = 1 on closedBall(0, 1) and tsupport φ₀ ⊆ ball(0, 2) (e.g. a smooth bump with inner radius 1 and outer radius 3/2), and let c₀ := sup ‖Dφ₀‖ < ∞. Let a := sup_z ‖ω(z)‖ and b := sup_z ‖Dω(z)‖ (finite, ω being smooth with compact support), and C' := (m + 1) C 2^{m+1} (b + c₀ a).

2. (Covering; uses μH[m](Z) = 0.) Let ε ∈ (0, 1). There are J ∈ ℕ, points p_1, …, p_J ∈ Z and radii σ_j ∈ (0, δ₀) with Z ⊆ ⋃_j B(p_j, σ_j) and Σ_j σ_j^m < ε. If m = 0: μH[0] is counting measure (μH[0]({x}) = 1), so Z = ∅ and J = 0 works. If m ≥ 1: let η' := min(ε 2^{−m−1}, (δ₀/2)^m). By the definition of the Hausdorff measure, μH[m](Z) = sup_{δ>0} inf {Σ_i diam(E_i)^m : Z ⊆ ⋃_i E_i countable, diam E_i ≤ δ}; since it is 0, there is a countable cover (E_i)_{i ≥ 1} of Z with diam E_i ≤ δ₀/2 and Σ_i diam(E_i)^m < η'. Discard the E_i not meeting Z, pick p_i ∈ E_i ∩ Z and set σ_i := diam(E_i) + (η' 2^{−i})^{1/m} > 0 (indices i ≥ 1, so (η' 2^{−i})^{1/m} ≤ 2^{−1/m} δ₀/2 < δ₀/2). Then E_i ⊆ B(p_i, σ_i), σ_i < δ₀, and Σ_i σ_i^m ≤ 2^{m−1} Σ_i (diam(E_i)^m + η' 2^{−i}) ≤ 2^m η' < ε. The open balls B(p_i, σ_i) cover the compact set Z; keep a finite subcover.

3. (Cut-off ζ, [D1].) Let φ_j(z) := φ₀((z − p_j)/σ_j): smooth, 0 ≤ φ_j ≤ 1, φ_j = 1 on B(p_j, σ_j), tsupport φ_j ⊆ B(p_j, 2σ_j), ‖Dφ_j‖ ≤ c₀/σ_j. Let ζ := ∏_{j=1}^J (1 − φ_j). Then ζ is smooth, 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1; ζ = 0 on the open set O_Z := ⋃_j B(p_j, σ_j) ⊇ Z; ζ = 1 on the open set ℝ^P ∖ ⋃_j tsupport φ_j; by the product rule and 0 ≤ 1 − φ_i ≤ 1, ‖Dζ‖ ≤ Σ_j ‖Dφ_j‖ ≤ Σ_j (c₀/σ_j) 1_{B(p_j, 2σ_j)}; and 1 − ζ ≤ Σ_j φ_j ≤ Σ_j 1_{B(p_j, 2σ_j)}. The forms ζω and (1 − ζ)ω belong to 𝒟^m(U) (smooth, tsupport ⊆ K) and ω = ζω + (1 − ζ)ω, so by linearity of d and of T₁: T₁(dω) = T₁(d(ζω)) + T₁(d((1 − ζ)ω)).

4. (T₁(d(ζω)) = 0; [D3] and book (2).) Let K₁ := closure(M₁) ∩ tsupport(ζω). Since ζω vanishes on the open set O_Z, tsupport(ζω) ⊆ K ∖ O_Z ⊆ K ∖ Z; hence K₁ ⊆ (closure(M₁) ∩ K) ∖ Z ⊆ M₁ by (h5), and K₁ is compact. By (h4) every z ∈ K₁ has G_z and c_z; choose z_1, …, z_L with K₁ ⊆ G_{z_1} ∪ … ∪ G_{z_L}. Choose an open O₁ with K₁ ⊆ O₁ ⊆ closure(O₁) ⊆ G_{z_1} ∪ … ∪ G_{z_L} and closure(O₁) compact, and a smooth partition of unity (ψ_l)_{l ≤ L} on the closed set closure(O₁) subordinate to (G_{z_l}) (Mathlib SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate): each ψ_l is smooth with tsupport ψ_l ⊆ G_{z_l}, and Σ_l ψ_l = 1 on closure(O₁). Put χ := Σ_l ψ_l.
 (a) The form (1 − χ)ζω vanishes on the open set O₁ ∪ (ℝ^P ∖ tsupport(ζω)), which contains M₁ (points of M₁ ∩ tsupport(ζω) lie in K₁ ⊆ O₁). Hence d((1 − χ)ζω) = 0 at every point of M₁ and, by (h2), T₁(d((1 − χ)ζω)) = 0.
 (b) For each l, ψ_l ζω ∈ 𝒟^m(U) and tsupport d(ψ_l ζω) ⊆ tsupport(ψ_l ζω) ⊆ tsupport ψ_l ⊆ G_{z_l}; by (h4) and (h1), T₁(d(ψ_l ζω)) = c_{z_l} T(d(ψ_l ζω)) = c_{z_l} ∂T(ψ_l ζω) = 0.
 Since ζω = (1 − χ)ζω + Σ_l ψ_l ζω, linearity gives T₁(d(ζω)) = 0.

5. (Error term; [D2].) Let F := (1 − ζ)ω. F vanishes on the open set ℝ^P ∖ ⋃_j tsupport φ_j, so dF(x) = 0 unless x ∈ ⋃_j B(p_j, 2σ_j). Since DF(x) = (1 − ζ(x)) Dω(x) − Dζ(x) ⊗ ω(x), ‖dF(x)‖ ≤ (m + 1) ‖DF(x)‖ ≤ (m + 1)((1 − ζ(x)) b + ‖Dζ(x)‖ a) ≤ s(x) := (m + 1) Σ_j (b + c₀ a/σ_j) 1_{B(p_j, 2σ_j)}(x). By (h2), |T₁(dF)| = |∫_{M₁} ξ(x)(dF(x)) dH^n| ≤ (∫⁻_{M₁} |ξ(x)(dF(x))| dH^n).toReal (this bound of a Bochner integral by the lower integral of its absolute value needs no integrability), and by (h3), |ξ(x)(dF(x))| ≤ ‖dF(x)‖ ≤ s(x) for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M₁. By (h6) at the points p_j ∈ Z ⊆ K with radii 2σ_j < r₁ (σ_j < δ₀ ≤ r₁/2):
 ∫⁻_{M₁} s dH^n = (m + 1) Σ_j (b + c₀ a/σ_j) H^n(M₁ ∩ B(p_j, 2σ_j)) ≤ (m + 1) Σ_j (b + c₀ a/σ_j) C (2σ_j)^{m+1} ≤ (m + 1) C 2^{m+1} (b + c₀ a) Σ_j σ_j^m ≤ C' ε,
 using σ_j ≤ 1 (so σ_j^{m+1} ≤ σ_j^m). Hence |T₁(dF)| ≤ C' ε.

6. By steps 3–5, |T₁(dω)| ≤ C' ε for every ε ∈ (0, 1), with C' independent of ε. Hence ∂T₁(ω) = T₁(dω) = 0. As ω ∈ 𝒟^m(U) was arbitrary, T₁.boundary = 0.
proof_key_steps: Cover the compact μH[n−1]-null set Z ⊇ (closure(M₁) ∩ spt ω) ∖ M₁ by finitely many balls B(p_j, σ_j) with Σ σ_j^{n−1} < ε and set ζ = ∏(1 − φ_j).
closure(M₁) ∩ spt(ζω) is a compact subset of M₁; a partition of unity subordinate to the proportionality neighbourhoods gives T₁(d(ζω)) = Σ_l c_l ∂T(ψ_l ζω) = 0.
The remainder T₁(d((1 − ζ)ω)) is at most n C 2^n (b + c₀a) Σ σ_j^{n−1} by the density bound.
Let ε → 0.

audit.reason: The covering supplies strictly admissible radii. The partition of unity proves the localized boundary identity, and the operator-norm estimate gives a finite O(ε) error. The unconditional Bochner-integral bound avoids an unstated integrability assumption. The argument includes m = 0 and empty covers.

subproblem.title: Mass of an integer multiplicity current: M_W(τ(M, θ, ξ)) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^n (Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3))
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open and let the IMRep R = (C, θ, ξ) in U represent T ∈ 𝒟_n(U). Then for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P, M_W(T) = R.measure(W) = ∫_{C∩W} θ dH^n, where M_W(T) is Simon's mass (6.2.5) with the Euclidean coefficient norm |·|_E on n-covectors (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = R.measure W
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–766, stated there without proof), Definition 3.1 (lines 733–753) and the mass (6.2.4)–(6.2.8). Notation: Λ^n is the space of n-covectors (continuous alternating n-forms on ℝ^P); for α ∈ Λ^n, |α|_E := (Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})²)^{1/2} (covectorEuclideanNorm); ev_τ(α) := α(τ_1, …, τ_n); μ := R.measure = θ H^n⌞C. A form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) is admissible if tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(z)|_E ≤ 1 for all z, and M_W(T) = sup ofReal T(ω) over admissible ω.

0. (Reduction and conventions.) Test forms in U have tsupport ⊆ U and C ⊆ U, so M_W(T) and μ(W) do not change if W is replaced by the open set W ∩ U. Assume W ⊆ U. All masses and measures are compared in [0, ∞]. The map α ↦ (α(e_I))_{I strictly increasing} is an injective linear map from Λ^n into a Euclidean space (an alternating n-form is determined by its values on increasing coordinate tuples), so |·|_E is the norm of an inner product on Λ^n; in particular its closed unit ball B_E is convex and the radial retraction onto B_E is 1-Lipschitz for |·|_E.

1. (Multilinear algebra.) (a) For every orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) in ℝ^P and α ∈ Λ^n, |α(τ)| ≤ |α|_E. (b) For every such τ there is β_τ ∈ Λ^n with |β_τ|_E = 1 and β_τ(τ) = 1.
 Proof. For an orthonormal basis f of ℝ^P put S_f(α) := Σ_{(j_1,…,j_n) ∈ {1,…,P}^n} α(f_{j_1}, …, f_{j_n})². (i) S_f(α) does not depend on f: change the basis in one slot at a time; with the other slots fixed, v ↦ α(…, v, …) is a linear functional λ and Σ_i λ(f_i)² = |λ|² = Σ_i λ(e_i)² (Parseval). (ii) S_e(α) = n! |α|_E²: index tuples with a repeated index contribute 0 (α is alternating), and each strictly increasing I is obtained from exactly n! injective tuples, each contributing α(e_I)². For (a), extend τ to an orthonormal basis f with f_i = τ_i (i ≤ n); then n! |α|_E² = S_f(α) ≥ Σ_{σ∈Sym(n)} α(τ_{σ(1)}, …, τ_{σ(n)})² = n! α(τ)². For (b), let β_τ(v_1, …, v_n) := det(⟨τ_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j=1..n} (the wedge of the covectors ⟨τ_i, ·⟩; SimonGMT Chapter06.wedgeCovectors_apply_det), an alternating n-form with β_τ(τ) = det I = 1. For the basis f above, β_τ(f_{j_1}, …, f_{j_n}) = ±1 if (j_1, …, j_n) is a permutation of (1, …, n) and 0 otherwise (a zero column if some j_k > n, two equal columns if an index repeats); so S_f(β_τ) = n! and |β_τ|_E = 1.
 Consequence: by the orientation condition of R, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ C we have ξ(x) = ±ev_τ for an orthonormal n-frame τ, hence |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α|_E for all α, and ξ(x)(±β_τ) = 1 with |±β_τ|_E = 1; that is, sup{ξ(x)(β) : |β|_E ≤ 1} = 1.

2. (M_W(T) ≤ μ(W).) If μ(W) = ∞ there is nothing to prove. Let ω be admissible. As tsupport ω is a compact subset of U, |θ ξ(ω)| ≤ θ 1_{tsupport ω} H^n-a.e. on C is integrable, and θ ξ(ω) vanishes off W. Hence T(ω) = R.action ω = ∫_C θ ξ(ω) dH^n ≤ ∫_{C∩W} θ |ξ(ω)| dH^n ≤ ∫_{C∩W} θ dH^n = μ(W). Taking the supremum over admissible ω, M_W(T) ≤ μ(W).

3. (M_W(T) ≥ μ(W).) Fix a real t < μ(W) and η ∈ (0, 1). If W ≠ ℝ^P let K_j := {z : |z| ≤ j, dist(z, ℝ^P ∖ W) ≥ 1/j} and O_j := {z : |z| < j + 1, dist(z, ℝ^P ∖ W) > 1/(2j)}; if W = ℝ^P let K_j := closedBall(0, j) and O_j := ball(0, j + 1). The K_j are compact and increase to W, so μ(K) > t for K := K_j with j large; put O := O_j. Then O is open, K ⊆ O, and closure(O) is a compact subset of W ⊆ U, so μ(K) ≤ μ(O) < ∞.
 3.1 (A Borel near-maximizing covector field.) Let ξ̃ be a Borel function with ξ̃ = ξ H^n-a.e. on C, and let {β_k}_{k≥1} be a countable dense subset of B_E := {β ∈ Λ^n : |β|_E ≤ 1}. By step 1 and the continuity of the linear map ξ̃(x), sup_k ξ̃(x)(β_k) = 1 for H^n-a.e. x ∈ C. Define recursively A_k := {x ∈ C ∩ K : ξ̃(x)(β_k) > 1 − η} ∖ ⋃_{i<k} A_i (disjoint Borel sets; (C ∩ K) ∖ ⋃_k A_k is H^n-null) and g := Σ_k 1_{A_k} β_k. Then g is Borel, |g|_E ≤ 1, g = 0 off K, and ξ(x)(g(x)) ≥ 1 − η for H^n-a.e. x ∈ C ∩ K; hence ∫_C θ ξ(g) dH^n ≥ (1 − η) μ(K).
 3.2 (Smooth admissible approximation.) ν := μ⌞O is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P (a Radon measure). By density of continuous compactly supported functions in L¹ of the finite (hence regular) Borel measure ν on ℝ^P, applied to the coordinates of g in a basis of Λ^n, there is a continuous compactly supported g₀ : ℝ^P → Λ^n with ∫ |g₀ − g|_E dν < η. Let χ ∈ C_c(O) with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1 and χ = 1 on K, and g₁ := χ g₀; since g = χ g (g = 0 off K), |g₁ − g|_E = χ |g₀ − g|_E ≤ |g₀ − g|_E, so g₁ is continuous with compact support in O and ∫ |g₁ − g|_E dν < η. Let π(v) := v / max(1, |v|_E) be the radial retraction onto B_E; it is 1-Lipschitz for the inner-product norm |·|_E (step 0) and fixes B_E, so g₂ := π ∘ g₁ is continuous with compact support in O, |g₂|_E ≤ 1 and |g₂ − g|_E ≤ |g₁ − g|_E pointwise. Mollify: h := g₂ * φ_ε (coordinatewise convolution with a mollifier φ_ε ≥ 0, ∫ φ_ε = 1, spt φ_ε ⊆ B_ε(0)), where ε < dist(spt g₂, ℝ^P ∖ O) is so small that sup_z |h(z) − g₂(z)|_E ≤ η/(1 + ν(ℝ^P)) (uniform continuity of g₂). Then h is C^∞ with compact tsupport h ⊆ O ⊆ W ⊆ U, and |h(z)|_E ≤ 1 for all z, since h(z) is an average of values of g₂ in the convex set B_E. Thus h is admissible for M_W(T), and ∫ |h − g|_E dν ≤ 2η.
 3.3 (Estimate.) h − g vanishes off O and |ξ(x)(v)| ≤ |v|_E for H^n-a.e. x ∈ C (step 1), so |T(h) − ∫_C θ ξ(g) dH^n| = |∫_C θ ξ(h − g) dH^n| ≤ ∫ |h − g|_E dν ≤ 2η. Therefore M_W(T) ≥ ofReal T(h) ≥ ofReal((1 − η) μ(K) − 2η) ≥ ofReal((1 − η) t − 2η) (μ(K) is finite). Letting η ↓ 0 and then t ↑ μ(W) (through real values; if μ(W) = ∞, t → ∞) gives M_W(T) ≥ μ(W).

4. By steps 2 and 3, T.massOn W = R.measure W for every open W.
proof_key_steps: Parseval in each slot shows the Euclidean coefficient norm is basis independent; hence |α(τ)| ≤ |α|_E and the wedge β_τ of the dual frame has |β_τ|_E = 1 and β_τ(τ) = 1.
Upper bound: T(ω) = ∫_C θ ξ(ω) ≤ ∫_{C∩W} θ dH^n for admissible ω.
Lower bound: a Borel near-maximizing covector field on a compact K ⊆ W, approximated in L¹(θH^n⌞C) by smooth admissible forms (density of C_c, radial retraction, mollification).

audit.reason: Slotwise Parseval and determinant covectors establish the correct coefficient-norm normalization. The upper estimate and smooth, norm-preserving L1 approximation establish equality for every open W, including infinite mass.

subproblem.title: Uniform upper mass bound from monotonicity with bounded generalized mean curvature (Simon Ch. 4, 3.17)
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open and let R = (C, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple (IMRep) in U whose associated varifold v(C, θ) has locally bounded generalized mean curvature in U (IMRep.HasLocallyBoundedMeanCurvature: δV(X) = −∫ X·H dμ for X ∈ C¹_c(U; ℝ^P), with H essentially bounded on compact subsets of U). Then for every compact K ⊆ U there are C₀ ∈ ℝ and r₁ > 0 such that μ(B_r(x)) ≤ C₀ r^n for all x ∈ K and 0 < r < r₁, where μ = R.measure = θ H^n⌞C.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.HasLocallyBoundedMeanCurvature → ∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ C r₁ : ℝ, 0 < r₁ ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → r < r₁ → R.measure (ball x r) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * r ^ n)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 4, 3.1–3.4 and 3.14–3.17 (chapter-04.txt lines 215–455), the monotonicity formula for varifolds with bounded generalized mean curvature, as used in the parent proof step 4 ('there are C, r₁ > 0 with μ_T(B_r(ξ')) ≤ Cr^n'). The book integrates the identity with an integrating factor; we use the same first-variation computation in differential-inequality form, which needs only |∫ X·H dμ| and is therefore independent of the sign convention for H (cf. the sign remark in SimonGMT Chapter04/MeanCurvature.lean). Because the contract's first variation is a Bochner integral, step 3 verifies that its integrand is integrable.

1. (Setup.) If K = ∅ there is nothing to prove (take C₀ = 0, r₁ = 1); assume K ≠ ∅. μ := R.measure = θ H^n⌞C is a Borel measure which is finite on compact subsets of U (∫_{C∩K'} θ dH^n < ∞ for compact K' ⊆ U). By hypothesis there is H such that for each compact K' ⊆ U some Λ' bounds |H| μ-a.e. on K', and for every C¹ vector field X with compact support in U, R.firstVariation X = −∫ X·H dμ, where R.firstVariation X = ∫_C θ div_C X dH^n with div_C X(z) := tr(P_z ∘ DX(z)) and P_z the orthogonal projection onto approxTangentPlane n C z. Choose δ ∈ (0, 1] such that K' := {z : dist(z, K) ≤ 3δ} ⊆ U (possible since K is compact and nonempty and dist(K, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 0 when U ≠ ℝ^P; any δ ∈ (0, 1] if U = ℝ^P); K' is compact. Let Λ := max(Λ', 0) for a bound Λ' of |H| μ-a.e. on K'. Put r₁ := δ and C₀ := e^{2Λδ} δ^{−n} μ(K') (a finite real number).

2. (Tangent planes.) Since 1 ≤ θ < ∞ on C, μ = θ H^n⌞C and H^n⌞C have the same null sets, so 'μ-a.e.' and 'H^n-a.e. on C' mean the same below. For μ-a.e. z we have z ∈ C and, by the orientation condition of R, a subspace Q_z and an orthonormal basis τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) of Q_z with R.orient z = ε ev_τ (ε = ±1, ev_τ(α) := α(τ_1, …, τ_n)) and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C z Q_z. By uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces (Simon Ch. 3, 1.5(1); SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), approxTangentPlane n C z = Q_z; so P_z = Σ_k τ_k ⟨τ_k, ·⟩, tr P_z = n, |P_z v| ≤ |v|, and tr(P_z ∘ L) = Σ_k ⟨τ_k, L τ_k⟩ for every linear L. At every z (also where no approximate tangent space exists, in which case approxTangentPlane n C z = ⊥ and P_z = 0), |tr(P_z ∘ L)| ≤ n ‖L‖.

3. (The first-variation integrand is integrable.) Let X be a C¹ vector field with compact support in U and L(z) := DX(z) (continuous). For a strictly increasing J = (j_1 < … < j_n) let e^J ∈ Λ^n be the coordinate covector e^J(u_1, …, u_n) := det(⟨e_{j_k}, u_l⟩)_{k,l} (the wedge of the coordinate 1-covectors), and for a linear map L and α ∈ Λ^n let L·α ∈ Λ^n be (L·α)(u_1, …, u_n) := Σ_k α(u_1, …, L u_k, …, u_n); L·α is continuous and multilinear, and alternating: if u_a = u_b for some a ≠ b, the terms with k ∉ {a, b} vanish and the terms k = a and k = b cancel by antisymmetry of α. Claim: for μ-a.e. z, div_C X(z) = Σ_J R.orient z (e^J) · R.orient z (L(z)·e^J). Proof: with z, τ, ε as in step 2, put β_τ(u) := det(⟨τ_i, u_l⟩)_{i,l}. Both β_τ and Σ_J ev_τ(e^J) e^J are alternating n-forms, and they agree on every increasing coordinate tuple e_{J'} := (e_{j'_1}, …, e_{j'_n}), because e^J(e_{J'}) = δ_{JJ'} and β_τ(e_{J'}) = det(⟨τ_i, e_{j'_l}⟩) = det(⟨e_{j'_k}, τ_l⟩) = e^{J'}(τ) = ev_τ(e^{J'}); an alternating n-form is determined by its values on increasing coordinate tuples (two such forms agreeing there agree on every injective coordinate tuple, a permutation of an increasing one, by the sign rule, and both vanish on coordinate tuples with a repeated vector; multilinearity then gives equality everywhere — Mathlib Basis.ext_alternating with AlternatingMap.map_perm), so β_τ = Σ_J ev_τ(e^J) e^J. Next, ev_τ(L·β_τ) = Σ_k β_τ(τ_1, …, L τ_k, …, τ_n) = Σ_k ⟨τ_k, L τ_k⟩ = tr(P_z ∘ L) (the k-th summand is the determinant of the identity matrix with its k-th column replaced by (⟨τ_i, Lτ_k⟩)_i). By linearity of α ↦ L·α, tr(P_z ∘ L) = Σ_J ev_τ(e^J) ev_τ(L·e^J) = Σ_J (ε ev_τ)(e^J) (ε ev_τ)(L·e^J), as ε² = 1. This proves the claim. Since R.orient is a.e. strongly measurable for H^n⌞C (with values in the finite-dimensional dual of Λ^n), z ↦ L(z)·e^J is continuous, and evaluation is jointly continuous, the right-hand side, hence z ↦ div_C X(z), is a.e. strongly measurable for H^n⌞C. Moreover |div_C X| ≤ n ‖DX‖_∞ everywhere and div_C X = 0 off spt X, so θ div_C X is H^n⌞C-integrable (θ is integrable on C ∩ spt X). Consequently R.firstVariation X = ∫_C θ div_C X dH^n = ∫ div_C X dμ is a genuine (absolutely convergent) integral.

4. (Radial test fields.) Fix φ ∈ C^∞(ℝ) nonincreasing with 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, φ = 1 on (−∞, 1] and φ = 0 on [2, ∞) (for instance φ(t) = s(2 − t) with s the standard smooth transition function). Fix x₀ ∈ K and ρ ∈ (0, δ]; with r(z) := |z − x₀| put X_ρ(z) := φ(r(z)/ρ)(z − x₀). X_ρ is C^∞ (φ(r/ρ) ≡ 1 for r < ρ, so the non-smoothness of r at x₀ plays no role) and spt X_ρ ⊆ closedBall(x₀, 2ρ) ⊆ K' ⊆ U.

5. (Divergence; Simon 3.2.) For z ≠ x₀, DX_ρ(z) = φ(r/ρ) Id + (φ'(r/ρ)/(ρ r)) (z − x₀) ⊗ (z − x₀). Hence for μ-a.e. z, div_C X_ρ(z) = n φ(r/ρ) + (r/ρ) φ'(r/ρ) |P_z ν|² with ν := (z − x₀)/r (and div_C X_ρ(x₀) = n = nφ(0)). Since φ' ≤ 0 and |P_z ν| ≤ 1: div_C X_ρ(z) ≥ n φ(r/ρ) + (r/ρ) φ'(r/ρ) for μ-a.e. z.

6. (Differential inequality.) Let I(ρ) := ∫ φ(|z − x₀|/ρ) dμ(z) for ρ ∈ (0, δ]. The ρ'-derivative of the integrand, −(r/ρ'²) φ'(r/ρ'), vanishes outside closedBall(x₀, 2ρ') and, for ρ' ∈ (ρ/2, δ), is bounded by (4 sup|φ'|/ρ)·1_{closedBall(x₀, 2δ)}(z), a μ-integrable function independent of ρ'; by dominated differentiation under the integral sign, I is differentiable at every ρ ∈ (0, δ) with ρ I'(ρ) = −∫ (r/ρ) φ'(r/ρ) dμ. Integrating the inequality of step 5 against μ (legitimate by step 3) and using step 1:
 n I(ρ) − ρ I'(ρ) ≤ ∫ div_C X_ρ dμ = −∫ X_ρ·H dμ ≤ ∫ φ(r/ρ) r |H| dμ ≤ 2ρΛ I(ρ),
 because r ≤ 2ρ where φ(r/ρ) ≠ 0 and |H| ≤ Λ μ-a.e. on K' ⊇ spt X_ρ (so X_ρ·H is bounded μ-a.e. on its compact support and integrable; the bound would hold trivially otherwise, a non-integrable Bochner integral being 0). Thus ρ I'(ρ) ≥ (n − 2Λρ) I(ρ) on (0, δ).

7. (Monotonicity; Simon 3.17.) g(ρ) := e^{2Λρ} ρ^{−n} I(ρ) satisfies g'(ρ) = e^{2Λρ} ρ^{−n−1} (ρ I'(ρ) − n I(ρ) + 2Λρ I(ρ)) ≥ 0 on (0, δ), and g is continuous on (0, δ]; hence g is nondecreasing on (0, δ].

8. (Conclusion.) Let 0 < r < δ. Since φ(|z − x₀|/r) = 1 on B_r(x₀) and φ ≥ 0, μ(B_r(x₀)) ≤ I(r) = e^{−2Λr} r^n g(r) ≤ r^n g(δ) = e^{2Λδ} δ^{−n} r^n I(δ) ≤ e^{2Λδ} δ^{−n} μ(closedBall(x₀, 2δ)) r^n ≤ C₀ r^n, because 0 ≤ φ(|z − x₀|/δ) ≤ 1_{closedBall(x₀, 2δ)}(z) and closedBall(x₀, 2δ) ⊆ K'. Since x₀ ∈ K was arbitrary, R.measure(ball x r) ≤ ofReal(C₀ r^n) for all x ∈ K and 0 < r < r₁ = δ.
proof_key_steps: Choose δ so that the closed 3δ-neighbourhood K' of K is a compact subset of U, and Λ bounding |H| μ-a.e. on K'.
The first-variation integrand is integrable: a.e. div_C X = Σ_J ξ(e^J)·ξ(DX·e^J) is measurable, and |div_C X| ≤ n‖DX‖_∞.
Radial fields X_ρ = φ(|z − x₀|/ρ)(z − x₀) satisfy div_C X_ρ ≥ nφ(r/ρ) + (r/ρ)φ'(r/ρ) a.e., since approximate tangent planes are n-dimensional.
The first variation identity gives ρI'(ρ) ≥ (n − 2Λρ)I(ρ) for I(ρ) = ∫ φ(r/ρ) dμ.
e^{2Λρ}ρ^{−n}I(ρ) is nondecreasing, so μ(B_r(x₀)) ≤ e^{2Λδ}δ^{−n}μ(K') r^n for r < δ.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 2 ('reg T is relatively open in spt T, and every z ∈ reg T has a ball B_r(z) with spt T ∩ B_r(z) = M' ∩ B_r(z) a connected C¹ graph …; (a) closure(M₁) ∖ M₁ ⊆ sing T; (b) …; on M₁, H^n(M₁ ∖ M) = 0 and ξ orients T_xM₁ a.e.'), Simon 7.4.1 (chapter-07.txt lines 590–612). The parent deduces T₁ = T near M₁ from θ = 1 a.e. (5.2(‡)); here only T₁ = |m_z|⁻¹·T near each z ∈ M₁ is proved, by uniqueness of the representation on a regular sheet, which is all the cut-off argument needs; 5.2(‡) is not used.
Notation: S := spt T = U ∖ Z(T), where Z(T) (zeroRegion) is the union of the open sets with compact closure in U on which T vanishes; Z(T) is open, so S is Borel and closure(S) ∩ U ⊆ S. reg := reg T ⊆ S and sing T = S ∖ reg. For z ∈ reg fix data (ρ_z, m_z, M_z, ξ_z) from the definition: ball(z, ρ_z) ⊆ U, m_z ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}, M_z an embedded C¹ n-submanifold with z ∈ M_z, oriented by ξ_z (continuous on M_z, each ξ_z(x) a unit orientation of T_xM_z), H^n(M_z ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ ball(z, ρ_z), and T(ω) = m_z ∫_{M_z} ξ_z(ω) dH^n whenever tsupport ω ⊆ ball(z, ρ_z). For an orthonormal n-frame τ let β_τ ∈ Λ^n be β_τ(v_1, …, v_n) := det(⟨τ_i, v_j⟩) (the wedge of the covectors ⟨τ_i, ·⟩; SimonGMT Chapter06.wedgeCovectors_apply_det), so β_τ(τ) = 1; a unit orientation ε·ev_τ (ε = ±1, ev_τ(α) = α(τ)) satisfies |ε ev_τ(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for all α and ε ev_τ(ε β_τ) = 1; in particular it is nonzero.

1. (Facts on an embedded C¹ n-submanifold M with a chart (V, W, ψ) at x ∈ M: V ⊆ ℝ^n and W ⊆ ℝ^P open, x ∈ W, ψ C¹ and injective on V with injective differential, ψ(V) = W ∩ M, and V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W.)
 (F1) ψ : V → W ∩ M is a homeomorphism, W ∩ M is relatively closed in W, and closure(M) ∩ W = M ∩ W. Proof: let F ⊆ V be relatively closed and let w ∈ W be a limit of ψ(f_j), f_j ∈ F. K := {ψ(f_j)} ∪ {w} is a compact subset of W, so the f_j lie in the compact set V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K); a subsequence converges to some v ∈ V; then v ∈ F and ψ(v) = w by continuity. So ψ maps relatively closed subsets of V to relatively closed subsets of W; with F = V, W ∩ M is relatively closed in W, and a continuous closed bijection V → W ∩ M is a homeomorphism. If x' ∈ closure(M) ∩ W, points of M converging to x' eventually lie in the open set W, so x' ∈ closure(W ∩ M) ∩ W = W ∩ M.
 (F2) H^n(ψ(B)) > 0 for every nonempty open B ⊆ V. Proof: fix v ∈ B, let L := Dψ(v) (injective), p the orthogonal projection onto L(ℝ^n), and Π := L⁻¹ ∘ p : ℝ^P → ℝ^n (linear, Lipschitz with constant ‖Π‖). Π ∘ ψ is C¹ near v with D(Π ∘ ψ)(v) = Id, so by the inverse function theorem it maps some open B' ⊆ B containing v onto a nonempty open set O ⊆ ℝ^n. Then 0 < L^n(O) = H^n(O) = H^n(Π(ψ(B'))) ≤ ‖Π‖^n H^n(ψ(B')) ≤ ‖Π‖^n H^n(ψ(B)). (μHE[n] = c_n·μH[n] with a constant c_n ∈ (0, ∞) depending only on n, so the Lipschitz image bound μH[n](Π(A)) ≤ Lip(Π)^n μH[n](A) (Mathlib LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le) carries over to H^n = μHE[n]; on ℝ^n, μHE[n] is Lebesgue measure, which is positive on nonempty open sets.)
 (F3) M is Borel: each x ∈ M has a chart set W_x with W_x ∩ M relatively closed in W_x (F1); countably many W_{x_i} cover M (Lindelöf), and M = ⋃_i (W_{x_i} ∩ closure(W_{x_i} ∩ M)).

2. (Local sheets.) For every z ∈ reg there is an open O_z with z ∈ O_z ⊆ ball(z, ρ_z) such that (a) S ∩ O_z = M_z ∩ O_z, (b) M_z ∩ O_z is connected, (c) S ∩ O_z ⊆ reg. Write ρ, m, M, ξ' for ρ_z, m_z, M_z, ξ_z.
 2.1 (S ∩ ball(z, ρ) ⊆ closure(M).) If x ∈ ball(z, ρ) ∖ closure(M), pick s > 0 with closedBall(x, s) ⊆ ball(z, ρ) ∖ closure(M). For tsupport ω ⊆ ball(x, s), T(ω) = m ∫_M ξ'(ω) dH^n = 0 since ω vanishes on M. So ball(x, s) (open, with compact closure in U) is a region where T vanishes: x ∈ Z(T), x ∉ S.
 2.2 (M ∩ ball(z, ρ) ⊆ S.) Let x ∈ M ∩ ball(z, ρ) and suppose x ∉ S; as x ∈ U, x ∈ Z(T), so T vanishes on some open W' ∋ x. Write ξ'(x) = ε ev_{τ'} and β := ε β_{τ'}, so ξ'(x)(β) = 1; by continuity of ξ' on M there is s > 0 with ξ'(x')(β) > 1/2 for all x' ∈ M ∩ ball(x, s). Take a chart (V_x, W_x, ψ_x) of M at x and O := ball(x, s) ∩ W' ∩ ball(z, ρ) ∩ W_x (open, x ∈ O). Let g ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P) with tsupport g ⊆ O, g ≥ 0, g(x) > 0, and ω := g β ∈ 𝒟^n(U). Then T(ω) = 0 because tsupport ω ⊆ W'. On the other hand V_x ∩ ψ_x⁻¹(O ∩ {g > 0}) is an open neighbourhood of ψ_x⁻¹(x) in ℝ^n (ψ_x is continuous on the open set V_x), so it contains a nonempty open ball B, and ψ_x(B) ⊆ M ∩ O ∩ {g > 0} has H^n(ψ_x(B)) > 0 by (F2). The integrand g ξ'(β) is ≥ 0 on M (g = 0 off ball(x, s)), > 0 on ψ_x(B), and integrable for H^n⌞M (bounded, vanishing off tsupport g, and H^n(M ∩ tsupport g) < ∞); M is Borel (F3), so the integral of a nonnegative integrable function that is positive on a set of positive measure is positive (Mathlib integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg_ae). Hence T(ω) = m ∫_M g ξ'(β) dH^n ≠ 0, a contradiction.
 2.3 (Construction of O_z.) Let (V, W, ψ) be a chart of M at z and v₀ := ψ⁻¹(z). Choose t > 0 with ball(v₀, t) ⊆ V and ψ(ball(v₀, t)) ⊆ ball(z, ρ). By (F1), ψ(ball(v₀, t)) is relatively open in W ∩ M, i.e. ψ(ball(v₀, t)) = O'' ∩ W ∩ M for some open O''. Put O_z := O'' ∩ W ∩ ball(z, ρ), an open set containing z. Then M ∩ O_z = ψ(ball(v₀, t)), the continuous image of a ball, hence connected: (b). By 2.1 and (F1), S ∩ O_z ⊆ closure(M) ∩ W ∩ O_z = M ∩ O_z, and M ∩ O_z ⊆ S by 2.2: (a).
 2.4 ((c).) Let x ∈ S ∩ O_z = M ∩ O_z and ρ' := ρ − |x − z| > 0. Then ball(x, ρ') ⊆ ball(z, ρ) ⊆ U, x ∈ M, and the same m, M, ξ' satisfy the local finiteness and representation requirements on ball(x, ρ') (compact subsets of ball(x, ρ') lie in ball(z, ρ), and forms supported in ball(x, ρ') are supported in ball(z, ρ)). Together with x ∈ S this gives x ∈ reg.

3. (Topology of M₁; (i), (iii), (iv).)

subproblem.title: Differences of integer multiplicity currents are integer multiplicity (Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(1))
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open and let S, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be integer multiplicity currents. Then S − T is integer multiplicity.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S T : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity S → IsIntegerMultiplicity T → IsIntegerMultiplicity (S - T)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(1) (chapter-06.txt lines 755–756, stated without proof), used in the parent proof step 5 ('S + T₂ is integer multiplicity (Ch. 6, 3.2(1))'). Uses the sibling approx_tangent_locality and uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces (Simon Ch. 3, 1.5(1); SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique). Notation: ev_τ(α) := α(τ_1, …, τ_n); a unit orientation of a subspace Q is ±ev_τ with τ an orthonormal basis of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf); for such ξ', |ξ'(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ ∏_i ‖τ_i‖ = ‖α‖ (operator norm), and ξ' ≠ 0 since ξ'(±β_τ) = 1 for β_τ(v) := det(⟨τ_i, v_j⟩).

1. (Data.) Let R_S = (C_S, θ_S, ξ_S) represent S and R_T = (C_T, θ_T, ξ_T) represent T. Then C := C_S ∪ C_T is Borel, ⊆ U, countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_iUnion), and for compact K ⊆ U, H^n(C ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{C_S∩K} θ_S dH^n + ∫_{C_T∩K} θ_T dH^n < ∞, as θ_S, θ_T ≥ 1 on their carriers.

2. (Common tangent planes on the overlap.) By approx_tangent_locality applied to C_S ⊆ C and to C_T ⊆ C: for H^n-a.e. x ∈ C_S, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C x Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C_S x Q for all Q, and likewise for C_T. Together with the orientation conditions of R_S and R_T and uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ C_S ∩ C_T the approximate tangent space Q_x of C at x exists and ξ_S(x), ξ_T(x) are both unit orientations of Q_x.

3. (Sign lemma.) If τ and τ' are orthonormal bases of the same n-dimensional subspace Q, then α(τ') = det(B) α(τ) for all α ∈ Λ^n, where B_{ij} := ⟨τ_i, τ'_j⟩, and det B = ±1. Indeed τ'_j = Σ_i B_{ij} τ_i; expanding multilinearly and using that α is alternating, α(τ') = Σ_{σ∈Sym(n)} sgn(σ) ∏_j B_{σ(j) j} · α(τ) = det(B) α(τ); and BᵀB = (⟨τ'_i, τ'_j⟩) = I, so det(B)² = 1. Consequently, by step 2, ξ_T(x) = ±ξ_S(x) for H^n-a.e. x ∈ C_S ∩ C_T.

4. (Measurable bookkeeping.) Let ξ̃_S, ξ̃_T be Borel functions with ξ̃_S = ξ_S H^n-a.e. on C_S and ξ̃_T = ξ_T H^n-a.e. on C_T. Let σ(x) := 1 if ξ̃_T(x) = ξ̃_S(x) and σ(x) := −1 otherwise (Borel). Then ξ_T = σ ξ_S H^n-a.e. on C_S ∩ C_T: at a.e. such x, ξ̃_S(x) = ξ_S(x), ξ̃_T(x) = ξ_T(x) and ξ_T(x) = ±ξ_S(x) (step 3); if ξ_T(x) = ξ_S(x) then σ(x) = 1, and otherwise ξ_T(x) = −ξ_S(x) and σ(x) = −1. For x ∈ C_S ∩ C_T let d(x) := θ_S(x) − σ(x) θ_T(x) ∈ ℤ. Define
 C' := (C_S ∖ C_T) ∪ (C_T ∖ C_S) ∪ {x ∈ C_S ∩ C_T : d(x) ≠ 0} (Borel);
 θ'(x) := θ_S(x) on C_S ∖ C_T, θ_T(x) on C_T ∖ C_S, |d(x)| on C_S ∩ C_T, and 0 elsewhere (Borel, ℕ-valued, ≥ 1 on C');
 ξ'(x) := ξ_S(x) on C_S ∖ C_T, −ξ_T(x) on C_T ∖ C_S, sign(d(x)) ξ_S(x) on C_S ∩ C_T (a.e. strongly measurable for H^n⌞C').

5. (R' := (C', θ', ξ') is an IMRep in U.) C' ⊆ C ⊆ U is Borel and countably n-rectifiable (subset of C). θ' ≤ θ_S + θ_T on C', so ∫_{C'∩K} θ' dH^n < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U. Orientation: C' is the union of the Borel pieces P₁ := C_S ∖ C_T ⊆ C_S, P₂ := C_T ∖ C_S ⊆ C_T and P₃ := C' ∩ C_S ∩ C_T ⊆ C_S. For P₁, apply approx_tangent_locality to P₁ ⊆ C_S and to P₁ ⊆ C' (H^n(C' ∩ K) ≤ H^n(C ∩ K) < ∞): for H^n-a.e. x ∈ P₁ the approximate tangent spaces of C_S, P₁ and C' at x coincide, and ξ'(x) = ξ_S(x) is a unit orientation of the one of C_S. Similarly for P₂ (with C_T and −ξ_T; −ev_τ is again a unit orientation, the definition allowing either sign) and for P₃ (with C_S and sign(d) ξ_S). Hence for H^n-a.e. x ∈ C' there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C' x Q and ξ'(x) a unit orientation of Q.

6. (R' represents S − T.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U). The functions θ_S ξ_S(ω) and θ_T ξ_T(ω) are bounded by θ_S ‖ω‖_∞ 1_{tsupport ω}, resp. θ_T ‖ω‖_∞ 1_{tsupport ω}, a.e. on their carriers, hence integrable, and (S − T)(ω) = ∫_{C_S} θ_S ξ_S(ω) dH^n − ∫_{C_T} θ_T ξ_T(ω) dH^n. Split both integrals over C_S ∖ C_T, C_T ∖ C_S and C_S ∩ C_T. On C_S ∩ C_T the combined integrand is a.e. θ_S ξ_S(ω) − θ_T σ ξ_S(ω) = d ξ_S(ω) = |d| sign(d) ξ_S(ω), which vanishes where d = 0. Therefore (S − T)(ω) = ∫_{C'} θ' ξ'(ω) dH^n = R'.action ω for every ω, so R' represents S − T and S − T is integer multiplicity.
proof_key_steps: On C_S ∩ C_T both orientations orient the common approximate tangent plane of C_S ∪ C_T (locality), so ξ_T = ±ξ_S there (an orthonormal change of frame has determinant ±1).
Carrier C' = (C_S △ C_T) ∪ {d ≠ 0}, multiplicity |θ_S − σθ_T| on the overlap, orientation sign(d)ξ_S; locality transfers the orientation condition to C'.
Splitting the integrals over the three pieces shows that R' represents S − T.

audit.reason: The declared locality dependency supplies common tangent planes. The measurable sign and multiplicity construction, carrierwise integrability, and integral calculation over the three pieces produce an IMRep representing exactly S − T.

subproblem.title: Restriction of an integer multiplicity current to a measurable part of its carrier: integrality and mass additivity
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let the IMRep R = (C, θ, ξ) in U represent T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), let A ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel with H^n(A ∖ C) = 0, and let T₁ ∈ 𝒟_n(U) satisfy T₁(ω) = ∫_A ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dH^n for all ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U). Then T₁ and T − T₁ are integer multiplicity, M_W(T₁) + M_W(T − T₁) = M_W(T) for every open W, and M_W(T − T₁) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U A : Set (Euclid P)) (T T₁ : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → MeasurableSet A → μHE[n] (A \ R.carrier) = 0 → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T₁ ω = ∫ x in A, R.orient x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μHE[n]) → IsIntegerMultiplicity T₁ ∧ IsIntegerMultiplicity (T - T₁) ∧ (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T₁.massOn W + (T - T₁).massOn W = T.massOn W) ∧ ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → (T - T₁).massOn W ≠ ∞
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 2 (last two sentences: 'T₁ = τ(M₁, 1, ξ) is integer multiplicity, T₂ := T − T₁ … is integer multiplicity, and μ_T = μ_{T₁} + μ_{T₂}, so M_W(T₁) + M_W(T₂) = M_W(T)'), Simon 7.5.11 proof (chapter-07.txt lines 990–995). The parent first shows θ = 1 on M₁; here only θ ≥ 1 is used: T − T₁ gets multiplicity θ − 1_A, which is the parent's τ(M ∖ M₁, θ, ξ) when θ = 1 on A. Uses the siblings approx_tangent_locality and imrep_mass_formula.

1. (Preliminaries.) θ ≥ 1 on C and ∫_{C∩K} θ dH^n < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, so H^n(C ∩ K) < ∞. For H^n-a.e. x ∈ C, ξ(x) = ±ev_τ with τ orthonormal, so |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for all α. Hence for ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) the functions θ ξ(ω) and ξ(ω) are bounded a.e. on C by θ ‖ω‖_∞ 1_{tsupport ω}, resp. ‖ω‖_∞ 1_{tsupport ω}, and are integrable on C.

2. (T₁ is integer multiplicity.) Let R₁ := (A ∩ C, 1, ξ). A ∩ C is Borel and ⊆ U; it is countably n-rectifiable as a subset of C; the constant multiplicity 1 is measurable and positive; ∫_{A∩C∩K} 1 dH^n ≤ ∫_{C∩K} θ dH^n < ∞; ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for H^n⌞(A ∩ C), a restriction of H^n⌞C. Orientation: by approx_tangent_locality applied to A ∩ C ⊆ C, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ A ∩ C, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n C x Q implies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (A ∩ C) x Q; combined with the orientation condition of R, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ A ∩ C, ξ(x) is a unit orientation of an approximate tangent space of A ∩ C at x. Since H^n(A ∖ C) = 0, T₁(ω) = ∫_A ξ(ω) dH^n = ∫_{A∩C} 1·ξ(ω) dH^n = R₁.action ω.

3. (T − T₁ is integer multiplicity.) Let C₂ := {x ∈ C : x ∉ A or θ(x) ≥ 2} (Borel) and θ₂ := θ − 1_A (truncated subtraction in ℕ: θ₂ = θ off A and θ₂ = θ − 1 on A). Then θ₂ ≥ 1 on C₂, θ₂ ≤ θ, and θ₂ = 0 on C ∖ C₂ = {x ∈ A ∩ C : θ(x) = 1}. R₂ := (C₂, θ₂, ξ) is an IMRep in U by the verifications of step 2 (orientation via approx_tangent_locality applied to C₂ ⊆ C). For ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), by step 1 and H^n(A ∖ C) = 0: (T − T₁)(ω) = ∫_C θ ξ(ω) dH^n − ∫_{C∩A} ξ(ω) dH^n = ∫_C (θ − 1_A) ξ(ω) dH^n = ∫_{C₂} θ₂ ξ(ω) dH^n = R₂.action ω, because on C the real function θ − 1_A equals θ₂ (θ ≥ 1) and θ₂ = 0 on C ∖ C₂.

4. (Mass additivity.) By imrep_mass_formula applied to R, R₁ and R₂, for every open W: M_W(T) = ∫_{C∩W} θ dH^n, M_W(T₁) = H^n(A ∩ C ∩ W), and M_W(T − T₁) = ∫_{C₂∩W} θ₂ dH^n = ∫_{C∩W} θ₂ dH^n. On C, θ = 1_A + θ₂ (as θ ≥ 1), so by additivity of the integral of nonnegative functions, ∫_{C∩W} θ dH^n = H^n(A ∩ C ∩ W) + ∫_{C∩W} θ₂ dH^n in [0, ∞]; that is, M_W(T₁) + M_W(T − T₁) = M_W(T).

5. (Finiteness.) If W is open and closure(W) is a compact subset of U, then M_W(T − T₁) = ∫_{C∩W} θ₂ dH^n ≤ ∫_{C∩closure(W)} θ dH^n < ∞.
proof_key_steps: R₁ = (A ∩ C, 1, ξ) and R₂ = (C₂, θ − 1_A, ξ) are IMReps; their orientation condition follows from locality of approximate tangent spaces for subsets of C.
They represent T₁ and T − T₁ because H^n(A ∖ C) = 0 and θ ≥ 1 on C.
By the mass formula M_W is ∫_{C∩W} of the multiplicity; θ = 1_A + (θ − 1_A) gives additivity, and local integrability gives finiteness.

audit.reason: Both constructed representations inherit approximate tangents through the declared locality dependency. Null-set removal and the multiplicity decomposition prove representation, mass additivity and local finiteness. No unproved multiplicity-one assertion is needed.

subproblem.title: Lemma 7.1.4 (decomposition lemma) in the competitor form of Definition 7.1.1
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, A ⊆ ℝ^P, and let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be minimizing in A (Simon 7.1.1, IsMinimizingIn). Let T₁ ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be such that T₁ and T − T₁ are integer multiplicity and, for every open W ⊂⊂ U, M_W(T₁) + M_W(T − T₁) ≤ M_W(T) and M_W(T − T₁) < ∞. Then T₁ is minimizing in A.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U A : Set (Euclid P)) (T T₁ : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → IsMinimizingIn T A → IsIntegerMultiplicity T₁ → IsIntegerMultiplicity (T - T₁) → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → T₁.massOn W + (T - T₁).massOn W ≤ T.massOn W) → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → (T - T₁).massOn W ≠ ∞) → IsMinimizingIn T₁ A
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon 7.1.4 and its proof (chapter-07.txt lines 62–79), in the competitor form of Definition 7.1.1 used by the contract (the same chain as SimonGMT Chapter07.minimizing_summands_source); parent proof step 5. Uses the sibling integer_multiplicity_sub. Write T₂ := T − T₁. (The hypothesis that T₂ is integer multiplicity, part of Simon's 1.4, is not needed below: integrality of the competitor comes from integer_multiplicity_sub.) Admissible forms for M_W are ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and Euclidean coefficient norm |ω(z)|_E ≤ 1 everywhere.

1. T₁ is integer multiplicity by hypothesis; it remains to check the minimality inequality.

2. Let W be open with W ⊂⊂ U, and let S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be integer multiplicity with SameBoundary S T₁ and spt(S − T₁) a compact subset of A ∩ W. Put S' := S − (T₁ − T) (that is, S + T₂). T is integer multiplicity (it is minimizing), so by integer_multiplicity_sub T₁ − T is integer multiplicity, and then so is S' = S − (T₁ − T).

3. S' − T = S − T₁ as currents (S'(ω) − T(ω) = S(ω) − T₁(ω) + T(ω) − T(ω)); hence spt(S' − T) = spt(S − T₁) is a compact subset of A ∩ W.

4. SameBoundary S' T: for n = 0 it holds by definition; for n = k + 1 and φ ∈ 𝒟^k(U), ∂S'(φ) = S(dφ) − T₁(dφ) + T(dφ) = ∂S(φ) − ∂T₁(φ) + ∂T(φ) = ∂T(φ), because ∂S = ∂T₁.

5. By the minimality of T in A, applied to W and S': M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S').

6. (Subadditivity.) For X, Y ∈ 𝒟_n(U), M_W(X − Y) ≤ M_W(X) + M_W(Y): if ω is admissible then so is −ω (|−α|_E = |α|_E, same support), and ofReal(X(ω) − Y(ω)) ≤ ofReal(X(ω)) + ofReal(Y(−ω)) ≤ M_W(X) + M_W(Y). Moreover M_W(T₁ − T) = M_W(T − T₁), since (T₁ − T)(ω) = (T − T₁)(−ω) and admissibility is invariant under ω ↦ −ω. Hence M_W(S') ≤ M_W(S) + M_W(T₂).

7. Combining with the hypothesis: M_W(T₁) + M_W(T₂) ≤ M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S') ≤ M_W(S) + M_W(T₂). Since M_W(T₂) < ∞ it may be cancelled in [0, ∞], giving M_W(T₁) ≤ M_W(S). As W and S were arbitrary, T₁ is minimizing in A.
proof_key_steps: For a competitor S of T₁, S' = S − (T₁ − T) is an integer multiplicity competitor of T with the same boundary and spt(S' − T) = spt(S − T₁).
Subadditivity of M_W and its invariance under negation give M_W(S') ≤ M_W(S) + M_W(T − T₁).
The superadditivity hypothesis and finiteness of M_W(T − T₁) allow cancellation: M_W(T₁) ≤ M_W(S).

audit.reason: The constructed competitor has the required boundary and support. Subtraction closure, mass subadditivity and finite ENNReal cancellation prove the exact competitor-based minimality statement. The redundant integrality hypothesis on T − T₁ is harmless.
